terms.meaning: a field the schema allows to be left out
the value the schema assumes when a field is left out
a special marker value that stands for something not present, here the missing marker
a value that means nothing is there

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Why optional fields are handled explicitly
sections.what: The header explains the two situations: a collection that defaults to empty, and a keyed block that is missing because it was never scored.

sections.name: list
sections.title: Empty list for a missing collection
sections.what: Returns an empty list when the collection is missing, and the collection itself otherwise.
sections.why: The schema defaults these collections to empty, so a missing one and an empty one mean the same thing.

sections.name: or
sections.title: Fallback for a scalar field
sections.what: Returns the fallback value when the field is missing, and the field itself otherwise. The header says it must only be used where absence does not matter.
sections.why: Applies a default the model documents, so the viewer does not invent its own.
sections.watch_out: Using it where absence matters would show a made-up value as if it were real. Also defines the missing marker.

sections.name: Maybe
sections.title: Type for a possibly missing value
sections.what: Defines a type that is either the real value or the missing marker.
sections.why: Lets the compiler make the code handle the missing case.

sections.name: present
sections.title: Marking an absent value
sections.what: Returns the missing marker when the value is undefined or null, and the value itself otherwise.
sections.why: Makes absence a finding that the page can show, rather than a value that passes silently.

sections.name: isMissing
sections.title: Checking for the missing marker
sections.what: Returns true only when the value is the missing marker.
sections.why: Lets the page branch to a missing-state message.

summary: Small helpers that handle fields the schema marks optional, so a missing value is handled on purpose rather than read as zero or as an empty value.
purpose: Stops the viewer from treating an absent value as a real zero, and from crashing when a field is missing.
why: The header says the wrong response to an optional field is a non-null shortcut at every use site. These helpers make the choice explicit at each place.
how: A list helper gives an empty list when a collection is missing. A default helper applies a documented fallback value. A present helper marks an absent value with a special marker, and a check helper tells whether a value is that marker.
inputs: Any value that may be undefined or null.
outputs: An empty list, the fallback value, the missing marker, or a yes or no answer.
risks: Using the default helper where absence matters would hide a defect. A missing keyed block should be marked missing, not shown as zero.
debug: If a page shows zero where a value should be missing, check whether the default helper was used there. If a page crashes on an undefined value, check whether the present helper wraps it.
